lesson.child_mission: Reading food labels means checking serve size, energy, sugar, salt and ingredient lists; compare products using the same serve ideas.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Why compare per 100 g instead of per whole tub sometimes?

FEEDBACK
Tub sizes differ; per 100 g is a fairer compare.

WATCH FOR
Ignoring serve size makes comparisons misleading.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Compare four labels using per 100 g where possible. Record two surprising findings.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teach_steps.explain:
Reading food labels means checking serve size, energy, sugar, salt and ingredient lists; compare products using the same serve ideas.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.
